content.text: José Virgilio Peña Suazo — "El Rey del Mambo" — is a Dominican singer, trumpeter, composer and bandleader from Cotuí, and the founder and lead voice of

, one of the longest-running merengue orchestras of the last three decades. Before he ever sang a note in public, he was already one of merengue's most in-demand writers and arrangers — his songs were hits for
and
. When
fired him one December, he decided to sing his own songs. He has not stopped since.
Cotuí and the trumpet

He grew up in limited circumstances in Cotuí, selling sweets on the street as a boy. He came to music at 17, with maestro Juan Eutimo Jerez, after his older brother Arturo — a trombonist — talked him into joining a company band at Rosario Dominicana, where the promise of a Cuban sandwich with fries and a soda got him studying solfège. He started on the tuba, then took up the trumpet. He studied accounting alongside; if he had not been a musician, he says, he would have been a bad accountant. In 1987 he moved to Santo Domingo and joined the Banda de Música del Cuerpo de Bomberos.
The arranger's years
He rose to first trumpet in
's orchestra, where
gave him his first break as a composer, recording «El Milloncito» for Cuco. He led
as musical director in 1989 — and wrote «El gato» for them, a song that would later become a cuarteto classic in Argentina in La Mona Jiménez's hands. In 1991 he joined
as trumpeter, composer and arranger («A usted lo botan», «La compota», «Penas de amores»), and in 1993 he moved to
and
's group. His songs were recorded by
(«Hoy Necesito Tenerla»),
(«La Pastilla») and
, among others. When he wrote for others, he sang the guide vocal in the studio himself — and reasoned that if a singer like
could learn a song from his reference, he could not sing so badly himself.
«Libre al fin»
The push to sing came when

let him go in a December. The beginnings were hard — musicians left because the band could not yet pay them a living. Then, at a small piano, he wrote the songs of «Libre al fin» in one sitting; released on 19 April 1994 with «Pa' los que sufren», the album caught on completely, and there, he says, he found his sound, free at last of the Coco Band and
influences.
was born.
The songwriter's catalogue
Peña Suazo has written more than five hundred compositions, by his own account. His own hits with
— «Pa' los que sufren», «Candela Pura», «Tú muere aquí», «Subido en el palo», «Mi mujer me gobierna» — sit alongside the songs he gave away: «El Milloncito» (
), «La Pastilla» (
), «Hoy Necesito Tenerla» (
), «El Cachetero» (Los Sabrosos del Merengue), «Un Chin Chin de Cariño» (Orquesta

), and the Coco Band songs. «Yo sé que Dios me tiene a mí lo mío», written during his mother's final illness, won Merengue del Año at the Premios Soberano in 2015. His «Que no se acabe el mambo» reached the soundtrack of Paolo Sorrentino's Oscar-winning «La grande bellezza» (2013) — he only learned of the placement when someone called him with the news. In Argentina, ten or twelve of his songs became cuarteto anthems in the hands of La Mona Jiménez, La Banda XXI, La Barra and La K'onga.
Public service and honours

From 2010 to 2020 he served as Viceministro de Cultura — ten years in public office. In December 2021 his «Mi mujer me gobierna» earned the band's first RIAA Gold record; in November 2025 he was inducted into the Galería del Merengue.
Family
His wife, Ebelise Fabián Reinoso, died on 2 August 2026. They had three children: Josi, Paola and José. His daughter Ivette Paola Peña designs all of his graphics and handles his bookings.
Legacy

Peña Suazo is one of the musicians who moved from the brass section to the front of the stage — and one of the few who brought a songwriter's catalogue with him. His arrangements for other orchestras accompany his own hits in the merengue of the nineties, and his songs keep travelling: to a film in Rome, to a cuarteto dance floor in Córdoba, to a new generation that found «Mi mujer me gobierna» on TikTok. He remains optimistic about the future of the genre: society, he says, keeps producing the men it needs.

Cotuí y la trompeta

Creció en condiciones humildes en Cotuí, vendiendo dulces en la calle de niño. Llegó a la música a los 17 años, con el maestro Juan Eutimo Jerez, después de que su hermano mayor Arturo — trombonista — lo convenciera de entrar a la banda de la empresa Rosario Dominicana, donde la promesa de un sándwich cubano con papas fritas y un refresco lo puso a estudiar solfeo. Empezó con la tuba y luego tomó la trompeta. Estudiaba contabilidad al mismo tiempo; si no hubiera sido músico, dice, habría sido un mal contador. En 1987 se mudó a Santo Domingo y entró en la Banda de Música del Cuerpo de Bomberos.

El catálogo del compositor
Peña Suazo ha escrito más de quinientas composiciones, según su propia cuenta. Sus éxitos con
— «Pa' los que sufren», «Candela Pura», «Tú muere aquí», «Subido en el palo», «Mi mujer me gobierna» — conviven con las canciones que regaló: «El Milloncito» (

Su «Que no se acabe el mambo» llegó a la banda sonora de «La grande bellezza» (2013), de Paolo Sorrentino, ganadora del Óscar — se enteró del uso cuando alguien lo llamó con la noticia. En Argentina, diez o doce de sus canciones se convirtieron en himnos del cuarteto en manos de La Mona Jiménez, La Banda XXI, La Barra y La K'onga.
Servicio público y honores

De 2010 a 2020 fue Viceministro de Cultura — diez años en un cargo público. En diciembre de 2021 su «Mi mujer me gobierna» le dio a la banda su primer disco de oro de la RIAA; en noviembre de 2025 fue exaltado a la Galería del Merengue.
Familia
Su esposa, Ebelise Fabián Reinoso, falleció el 2 de agosto de 2026. Tuvieron tres hijos: Josi, Paola y José. Su hija Ivette Paola Peña diseña toda su gráfica y maneja sus contrataciones.
Legado

Peña Suazo es de los músicos que pasaron de la sección de metales al frente del escenario — y de los pocos que llegaron con un catálogo de compositor bajo el brazo. Sus arreglos para otras orquestas acompañan a sus propios éxitos en el merengue de los noventa, y sus canciones siguen viajando: a una película en Roma, a una pista de cuarteto en Córdoba, a una generación nueva que encontró «Mi mujer me gobierna» en TikTok. Sigue optimista sobre el futuro del género: la sociedad, dice, va pariendo los hombres que necesita.
La Banda Gorda is a Dominican merengue orchestra founded in 1994 by

, its lead singer, composer, arranger and general director — and, for thirty-two years, its only constant member. It is one of the longest-running merengue orchestras of the last three decades: twenty-one studio albums, a Soberano for Merengue del Año, a RIAA Gold record, and a catalogue that travelled from Cotuí to a Sorrentino film and to the cuarteto dance floors of Argentina.
«Libre al fin»
came to the group as one of merengue's most in-demand writers and arrangers — first trumpet in
's orchestra, musical director of
, trumpeter and songwriter for
and
. When

fired him one December, he decided to sing his own songs. At a small piano he wrote the songs of «Libre al fin» in one sitting; released on 19 April 1994 with «Pa' los que sufren», the album caught on completely, and there, he says, he found his sound. The beginnings were hard — musicians left because the band could not yet pay them a living — but the records came almost one a year: «Durísimo... Candela Pura» (1995), the breakthrough; «Tú muere aquí» (1996); «Calienta esto» (1998); «Aquí, pero allá» (1999); «Esta noche» (2000); «Melao» (2002); «Puro mambo» (2004). The pianist and co-producer Manole Pérez was the group's musical director for four of those early years, tracing its musical line alongside
before leaving to found La Banda del Truco.
The hits

The group's merengue takes from mambo and from street sayings. «Subido en el palo», written for the envious — recorded five times before he was satisfied — became the official campaign song of Leonel Fernández's 2008 re-election and has been used by several parties since. «Yo sé que Dios me tiene a mí lo mío», written during his mother's final illness, won Merengue del Año at the Premios Soberano in 2015. «Mi mujer me gobierna» (2016) went viral on TikTok and earned the band's first RIAA Gold record in December 2021. «Que no se acabe el mambo», from «Puro mambo» (2004), reached the soundtrack of Paolo Sorrentino's Oscar-winning «La grande bellezza» (2013).
Argentina and the cuarteto
The group's songs found a second life in Argentina, where ten or twelve of
's compositions became cuarteto anthems in the hands of La Mona Jiménez, La Banda XXI, La Barra and La K'onga — it began with «El gato», written for
. In November 2024 the band played two concerts in Córdoba and Río Cuarto, to more than 1,900 people; La Voz de Córdoba called the visit "histórica".
Thirty years and counting
In September 2022 the band shared a bill with

for the first time; in February 2024 it celebrated «30 años, mi historia musical» at the Hard Rock Café in Santo Domingo. The nineteenth production, «La No. 19» (2022), gathered fifteen songs written during the Covid-19 lockdown. In November 2025
was inducted into the Galería del Merengue, and the band released its latest album, «La Química Perfecta». It remains active, led by its founder.
Legacy

La Banda Gorda is the sound of a songwriter who became a singer: a brass player's orchestra, built on arrangements and on songs written to be danced to and quoted in the street. Thirty-two years in, it is still the band that plays «Pa' los que sufren» because the audience will not let it leave without it.

Los éxitos

El merengue del grupo toma del mambo y de los dichos de la calle. «Subido en el palo», escrita para los envidiosos — grabada cinco veces antes de quedar satisfecho — fue la canción oficial de campaña de la reelección de Leonel Fernández en 2008 y la han usado varios partidos desde entonces. «Yo sé que Dios me tiene a mí lo mío», escrita durante la enfermedad final de su madre, ganó Merengue del Año en los Premios Soberano de 2015. «Mi mujer me gobierna» (2016) se viralizó en TikTok y le dio a la banda su primer disco de oro de la RIAA en diciembre de 2021. «Que no se acabe el mambo», de «Puro mambo» (2004), llegó a la banda sonora de «La grande bellezza» (2013), de Paolo Sorrentino, ganadora del Óscar.

Treinta años y contando
En septiembre de 2022 la banda compartió cartel con

por primera vez; en febrero de 2024 celebró «30 años, mi historia musical» en el Hard Rock Café de Santo Domingo. La producción número diecinueve, «La No. 19» (2022), reunió quince canciones escritas durante el confinamiento por el Covid-19. En noviembre de 2025
fue exaltado a la Galería del Merengue, y la banda lanzó su álbum más reciente, «La Química Perfecta». Sigue activa, dirigida por su fundador.
Legado

La Banda Gorda es el sonido de un compositor que se hizo cantante: una orquesta de trompetista, construida sobre arreglos y sobre canciones hechas para bailar y para citar en la calle. Treinta y dos años después, sigue siendo la banda que toca «Pa' los que sufren» porque el público no la deja irse sin ella.
